python_task_v1.prompt_instructions: Implement this Python learning task as a SINGLE self-contained Python file (task.py). Do NOT create separate test files or README. The script itself is the test. Include all required functions AND a complete `if __name__ == '__main__':` block that: (1) runs self-checks (unit-like tests), (2) prints clear metrics or pass/fail summaries, (3) asserts quality thresholds and exits non-zero on failure. Prefer standard library only unless the task explicitly allows third-party libs. If optional dependencies are missing, provide a graceful fallback path while still verifying correctness.
evaluation_rules: The `self_check()` function MUST validate correctness with deterministic tests (use seed). It MUST raise AssertionError on failure.
The `run()` function MUST execute the main logic and return a dict of results/metrics.
The `if __name__ == '__main__':` block MUST call set_seed(), run(), self_check(), print results, save_artifacts(), and exit 0 on success or non-zero on failure.
No external test runner. No separate test files.
docstring_rules: Top-level module docstring must include: purpose, inputs/outputs, and at least 1 example usage snippet.

tasks.description: Implement small pure functions exercising ints/floats/strings/bools, conditionals, loops, and basic error handling. Include deterministic self-checks.

requirements.implementation: Write functions: safe_div(a,b)->float|None, fizzbuzz(n)->list[str], summarize(nums)->dict(min,max,mean). Use only stdlib.
requirements.edge_cases: safe_div must handle b==0 without throwing; fizzbuzz must validate n>=1; summarize must handle empty list by raising ValueError.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must cover at least 12 assertions, including edge cases.
requirements.main_block: Print summary of passed checks + example outputs; exit non-zero on failure.
requirements.output: Return dict with counts of checks run, checks passed, and example outputs.

tasks.description: Implement a small library of functions with type hints, docstrings, and demonstrate local/global/nonlocal scope behavior safely.

requirements.implementation: Functions: normalize_text(s)->str, word_count(s)->dict[str,int], make_power(k)->callable. Use closures for make_power.
requirements.style: All public functions must have type hints and docstrings with examples.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must verify correctness on punctuation/whitespace cases and closure behavior.
requirements.output: Return dict with sample transformed text and top-k words.

tasks.description: Implement utility functions that manipulate Python data structures and demonstrate complexity-aware choices.

requirements.implementation: Functions: dedupe_preserve_order(xs), invert_mapping(d), group_by_key(items,key_fn).
requirements.evaluation: self_check must include randomized tests with fixed seed and compare against reference implementations.
requirements.output: Return dict with sizes and a few example groups.

tasks.description: Generate synthetic records, write to JSON and CSV, then read back and validate round-trip integrity.

requirements.data: Create 200 records with fields: id(int), name(str), score(float), tags(list[str]).
requirements.implementation: Write/read JSON and CSV (CSV stores tags as ';'-joined string). Use tempfile and pathlib.
requirements.evaluation: Round-trip must preserve ids and scores within 1e-9; tags must match exactly after CSV decoding.
requirements.artifacts: Save outputs to tasks/<task_id>/artifacts/records.json and records.csv.

tasks.description: Build a small domain model using dataclasses, validation, and rich repr/ordering.

requirements.implementation: Create dataclass Student(name:str, sid:int, grades:list[float]) with methods: average(), letter_grade(). Validate grade range [0,100].
requirements.evaluation: self_check must validate ordering by sid, average correctness, and validation failures.
requirements.output: Return dict with class roster stats (mean, min, max).

tasks.description: Implement streaming computations with generators to avoid loading all data into memory.

requirements.implementation: Generator: read_numbers_from_text(text)->yield floats; sliding_window(iterable,k)->yield tuples; moving_average(iterable,k)->yield floats.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must verify laziness by processing large synthetic stream and not materializing the whole list (use counters/limited peeks).
requirements.output: Return dict with first/last few moving averages and count processed.

tasks.description: Implement a custom context manager for timing and for safe temporary directory handling.

requirements.implementation: Create @contextmanager timer(name) yielding start_time and capturing elapsed; create class TempDir context manager (mkdtemp + cleanup).
requirements.evaluation: self_check must assert temp dir removed after exit and timer reports positive elapsed.
requirements.artifacts: Save a small timing report JSON.

tasks.description: Design robust error handling and structured logs for a mini ETL pipeline.

requirements.implementation: Parse mixed-quality lines into records; invalid lines go to 'rejects' with reason codes; use logging with timestamps and levels.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must inject at least 5 malformed cases and verify reasons and counts.

tasks.description: Implement decorators for memoization and call tracing while preserving metadata.

requirements.implementation: Decorator memoize(maxsize=None) and trace_calls(logger_fn). Use functools.wraps.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must verify cache hits reduce call count and __name__/__doc__ preserved.
requirements.output: Return dict with call counts and cache stats.

tasks.description: Design interfaces using typing.Protocol and implement two concrete classes.

requirements.implementation: Define Protocol Serializer with dumps/loads; implement JsonSerializer and CsvSerializer (for simple list-of-dicts).
requirements.evaluation: self_check must round-trip multiple schemas and validate type hints exist for public APIs.
requirements.output: Return dict with encoded sizes and round-trip success flags.

tasks.description: Benchmark CPU-bound and I/O-bound workloads using threading and multiprocessing; report speedups.

requirements.implementation: CPU task: count primes up to N; IO task: simulate downloads via sleep + small writes. Implement sequential, threading, multiprocessing versions.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must validate correctness of prime counts and that MP outperforms sequential by a minimum factor for CPU-bound (configurable small N).

tasks.description: Build an asyncio pipeline with backpressure using queues, tasks, and cancellation handling.

requirements.implementation: Async producer generates items; consumers process with variable latency; ensure clean shutdown and no leaked tasks.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must assert all items processed exactly once and pipeline terminates under timeout.
requirements.output: Return dict with throughput (items/sec) and processed counts.

tasks.description: Implement stable merge sort and binary search with thorough correctness checks vs Python's sorted().

requirements.implementation: merge_sort(xs,key=None)->list; binary_search(sorted_xs,target)->index|(-1).
requirements.evaluation: self_check must run randomized tests and verify stability property with (key,value) pairs.
requirements.metrics: Report comparisons count estimate and runtime for increasing sizes.

tasks.description: Implement an LRU cache with O(1) get/put using OrderedDict; verify eviction correctness.

requirements.implementation: Class LRUCache(capacity) with get/put; track hits/misses.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must include a reference simulation and randomized operation sequences.
requirements.output: Return dict with hit rate and final keys.

tasks.description: Implement BFS shortest path in unweighted graphs and Dijkstra for weighted graphs using heapq.

requirements.implementation: Represent graph via adjacency dict; implement bfs_path(graph,s,t) and dijkstra(graph,s).
requirements.evaluation: self_check must test on known graphs and randomized small graphs (compare dijkstra to brute force for tiny graphs).
requirements.output: Return dict with path lengths and example paths.

tasks.description: Solve edit distance (Levenshtein) with DP, plus memory-optimized variant; compare results and speed.

requirements.implementation: edit_distance(a,b)->int; edit_distance_optimized(a,b)->int using O(min(n,m)) memory.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must compare both methods across randomized strings and known examples.
requirements.artifacts: Save a small report comparing runtimes and memory use estimates.

tasks.description: Replace Python loops with NumPy vectorization and quantify speedup while preserving correctness.

requirements.implementation: Compute pairwise distances between points (N x 2) with (1) pure Python loops and (2) vectorized NumPy. Verify max error < 1e-9.
requirements.evaluation: self_check must assert vectorized is faster than loops by a minimum factor for N>=2000 (use time.perf_counter; allow slack).
requirements.artifacts: Save timings JSON and a small histogram of distances (matplotlib optional).

tasks.description: Use numba.njit to accelerate a numeric kernel; provide fallback if numba unavailable.

requirements.dependencies: numpy required; numba optional but recommended.
requirements.implementation: Kernel: 2D convolution (valid) on float32 arrays. Implement numpy baseline and numba-jit version.
requirements.evaluation: If numba present, assert speedup >= 1.5x for medium size; always assert numerical agreement within tolerance.

tasks.description: Implement a GPU/CPU dual-path array computation (e.g., batched matmul + softmax) using CuPy if available, otherwise NumPy.

requirements.implementation: Detect backend; run identical computation on both when possible and compare outputs (CPU reference).
requirements.evaluation: Always validate correctness; if cupy available, report GPU timing and assert it runs end-to-end.
requirements.output: Return dict with backend used, timings, and max error vs reference.

tasks.description: Build a numeric workload with PyTorch tensors and benchmark CPU vs CUDA if available; optionally torch.compile if present.

requirements.implementation: Workload: fused MLP-like ops (matmul + gelu + layernorm-ish) on random tensors; benchmark multiple runs with warmup.
requirements.evaluation: Always validate deterministic shapes and finite outputs; if CUDA available, assert CUDA is faster than CPU for large tensors (allow slack).
requirements.artifacts: Save benchmark_results.json with device info and timings.
